subject: music
topicDisplay: Area of Study 5: Conventions of Pop
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a standard 12-bar blues, which three chords are used?
questions.explain: The 12-bar blues is built on the tonic (I), subdominant (IV) and dominant (V) chords.

questions.q: In which decade did rock and roll first emerge as a popular style?
questions.explain: Rock and roll developed in the 1950s, drawing on blues, country and rhythm and blues.

questions.q: What is a riff?
options: A short, repeated melodic or rhythmic pattern
A long solo improvised over the whole song
The final chord of a piece
questions.explain: A riff is a short, catchy pattern that is repeated, often forming the basis of a song.

questions.q: Which rhythmic feature is most characteristic of reggae?
options: Chords played only on the first beat
A walking bass on every quaver
Brass stabs on beat one of every bar
questions.explain: Reggae is defined by its offbeat guitar or keyboard chords, known as the skank.

questions.q: What is a 'hook' in a pop song?
options: A short, catchy musical idea designed to be memorable
The opening bars played before the vocals begin
A gradual slowing of the tempo at the end
The lowest note sung in the chorus
questions.explain: A hook is a memorable phrase, riff or lyric that catches the listener's attention.

questions.q: What is the 'middle 8' in a typical pop song structure?
options: A contrasting section, often eight bars long, providing variety
The eight bars that open every verse
The introduction before the first verse
questions.explain: The middle 8 (or bridge) provides contrast, usually before returning to a final chorus.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation MIDI stand for?
questions.explain: MIDI is a protocol that lets electronic instruments and computers communicate.

questions.q: What does the effect 'reverb' do to a sound?
options: Adds a sense of space or ambience by simulating reflections
Raises the pitch by one octave
Splits the sound into left and right channels
questions.explain: Reverb simulates sound reflections in a space, adding depth and ambience.

questions.q: Which best describes the effect of a walking bass line in blues or rock and roll?
options: It drives the music forward with steady, mostly stepwise movement
It plays a single sustained note throughout
It doubles the vocal melody exactly
It plays only on the first beat of each bar
questions.explain: A walking bass moves steadily, usually by step, giving momentum to the harmony.

questions.q: Motown is most closely associated with which style of music?
questions.explain: Motown is a record label famous for its polished soul and pop sound.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the chorus in verse-chorus form?
options: It usually keeps the same words and music each time and contains the main hook
It changes both words and music every time it appears
It is always instrumental with no vocals
It appears only once, at the very end of the song
questions.explain: The chorus is typically repeated with the same lyrics and music and carries the hook.

questions.q: What is the main function of a pre-chorus?
options: To build anticipation and link the verse to the chorus
To end the song with a fade-out
To provide a lengthy instrumental solo
questions.explain: A pre-chorus creates tension and momentum, leading the listener into the chorus.

questions.q: Distortion is an effect most associated with which instrument in rock music?
questions.explain: Distortion overloads the signal to create the gritty, powerful electric guitar sound of rock.

questions.q: What is meant by overdubbing?
options: Recording additional parts on top of previously recorded tracks
Playing all instruments live at the same time
Deleting a track from a recording
Turning down the volume of the vocals
questions.explain: Overdubbing adds new layers to an existing recording, part of multitrack production.

questions.q: A song described as 'strophic' has which structure?
options: The same music repeated for each verse
A completely different melody in every bar
Only a chorus and no verses
questions.explain: In strophic form the same music is repeated for successive verses with different lyrics.

questions.q: What does a sampler do?
options: Stores and plays back recorded sounds, often triggered by keys or pads
questions.explain: A sampler records short sounds (samples) that can be triggered and manipulated in a track.

questions.q: A song runs: Intro – Verse – Chorus – Verse – Chorus – Middle 8 – Chorus. Which section provides contrast before the final chorus?
questions.explain: The middle 8 introduces contrasting material before the song returns to its final chorus.

questions.q: A producer wants a vocal to sound as though it is being sung in a large hall. Which effect should they add?
questions.explain: Reverb simulates the reflections of a large space, giving the vocal a hall-like ambience.

questions.q: A songwriter wants a guitar phrase to repeat as a distinct echo a short moment after it is played. Which effect is most suitable?
questions.explain: Delay (echo) repeats the signal after a set time, creating distinct repetitions of the sound.

questions.q: A track has a relaxed four-beat feel, offbeat guitar chords and a prominent bass line. Which style is it most likely to be?
questions.explain: Offbeat chords with a prominent bass and relaxed feel are hallmarks of reggae.
